sections.name: LoginPage (part 1)
sections.title: Sign-in form logic
sections.what: Holds the email, password, error and loading values. On submit, it sends the details to the login route, shows any error, and on success moves to the home page and refreshes it.
sections.why: Likely reason: the server checks the password, so this page only shows the server's answer.
sections.watch_out: The password is sent in the request, so the site must use HTTPS to keep it private.

sections.name: LoginPage (part 2)
sections.title: Email and password form
sections.what: Draws the CareerOS heading, error box, email and password fields, the sign-in button, and a link to create an account.
sections.why: Gives the user the form that the logic above drives.
sections.watch_out: The link text asks for an invite code, so the register page must check one.

summary: The sign-in screen. It sends the email and password to the login route and moves the user to the home page on success.
purpose: Lets the user sign in to their CareerOS account.
why: Likely reason: sign-in needs a form in the browser that talks to the server, and the server decides whether the password is correct.
how: 1. The user types an email and password. 2. Pressing sign in stops the normal page reload and sets a loading state. 3. The details are sent to the login route. 4. If the route refuses, its error is shown. 5. On success, the user is sent to the home page and the page data is refreshed. 6. The loading state is cleared.
inputs: The email and password typed by the user.
outputs: Either the home page after a successful sign-in, or an error message on the screen.
risks: All real checks happen in the login route, which is not visible here. Error text comes from the server. No limit on repeated attempts is visible in this file.
debug: If sign-in fails with no clear message, check the response shape from the login route. If the message says network error, check that the route can be reached. If the button stays on SIGNING IN, check that the request finishes. Session creation is in the login route, not this file.
